origin.description: Provenance label recorded by the installer or channel metadata.

CredentialEventType.description: Boundary that observed or injected credential material.

truncated.description:
The guest produced more output than the per-exec cap allows, so
`stdout` is a prefix. Defaulted so an older client still decodes.

FileListEntry.description: A single entry in a workspace file listing.

HostLogSource.description: Symbolic host log streams. Paths supplied by clients are never accepted.

provider.description: Provider identifiers and model names are open namespaces.

kind.description: Profile-owned artifact label, not a lifecycle or permission state.

cpus.description:
CPU count. If absent, service resolves from the selected profile's VM
resources.

env.description: Environment variables to inject into the guest at boot.

from.description:
Sandbox to clone state from. If provided, the new sandbox's session will
be cloned from this existing persistent sandbox.

persistent.description: When true, the VM is persistent (named VMs). Ephemeral VMs are destroyed on stop.

ram_mb.description:
RAM in megabytes. If absent, service resolves from the selected
profile's VM resources.

uds_path.description:
The UDS path the per-VM capsem-process is listening on. Clients MUST
use this value rather than recomputing it -- the service may fall back
to a short hashed path under /tmp/capsem-<uid>/ when the preferred path
would exceed SUN_LEN. See capsem_foundation::uds::instance_socket_path.

authentication.description:
The restarted gateway rotates its token. Obtain fresh credentials and
construct a new SDK client; never replay the restart mutation.

oneOf.description:
Session summaries returned by /info when the ledger is ready.
Missing summaries are accompanied by session_db readiness/error details.

can_resume.description:
True only when an inactive persistent VM can be started/resumed with
the currently installed profile and pinned assets.

last_error.description:
Short tail of `process.log` from the last failed boot. Populated
only when `status == VmLifecycleState::Defunct`. Renders in `capsem list` /
`capsem status` so a crashed VM tells the user *why* without
requiring a separate `capsem logs <id>` round-trip.

resume_blocked_reason.description:
Human-readable reason `can_resume` is false for an inactive persistent
VM, e.g. profile payload hash drift after an upgrade.

size_bytes.description:
On-disk size of the session dir in bytes. Populated for /info on
persistent VMs; useful for verifying that fork produced a compact
overlay and not a bloated sparse file.

StopResponse.description: Stop completes after the VM process exits. Persistent workspace state remains.

oneOf.description: Exit code for exec, HTTP code for net/model, decision for tool, null for fs.

VmActionResponse.description: Acknowledgement returned after a VM pause or deletion completes.

VmAiInfo.description: Recorded model and tool activity for this VM's session.

mcp.description: Recorded MCP tool calls, grouped by server and tool identity.

models.description: Models observed in the session, grouped by provider and model identity.

VmFilesInfo.description: Recorded filesystem activity, not a recursive workspace inventory.

VmStatsDetailResponse.description:
Latest retained events (200 per model/tool/network/file family, 100 per
process/audit/credential family), session model totals, and captured bodies.
This is a bounded inspection report; it is not the complete session ledger.

body_blobs.description: Captured request/response bodies grouped by event ID.

last_error.description:
Why a crashed VM died: the `process.log` tail the service captured.
The service splits the two on purpose -- a defunct session carries its
reason here and leaves `resume_blocked_reason` empty -- so a consumer
that reads only the latter has nothing to show for the one state where
the user most needs a reason.
